chunks: Of all these there was not one who did not deny the messengers. So My retribution was justified.
ai.seo_question: Why was God's retribution justified against the previous nations?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Sad, this verse underscores the cumulative consequence of rejecting divine messengers, a theme central to Shia exegesis regarding the continuity of prophetic guidance. It serves as a theological justification for divine retribution, linking the specific denial of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the historical patterns of earlier nations. This reinforces the Shia understanding of 'Adl (Divine Justice) as the basis for punishment being both deserved and proportionate to the consistent rejection of truth.
